Exact rolling min/max ports (scipy ndimage filters): NaN inputs diverge from pandas rolling min_periods=N (any NaN window -> NaN in pandas, inconsistent in scipy). Guard np.isnan(high/low).any() and fall back to the pandas path; NaN close needs no guard (only poisons its own row on both paths). Test with random 0-3 NaN frames.
Haiku 5.5 agents run only at effort high or xhigh — never lower, never max (user rule). reviewer-lite.md pins effort: high; pass effort explicitly when spawning any Haiku agent.

pandas 3.0.3 rolling(window).sum() is a Kahan-compensated running add/remove plus an all-same-value shortcut (GH#42064: prev_value*nobs) — NO numpy reduction matches it bitwise (window sum, running add/sub, Neumaier, cumsum diff all fail). A Python replica CAN match bitwise but is slower than pandas' C loop, so in exact ports keep just that op on pandas and vectorise the rest; Python-float list recurrences are bitwise-equal to numpy-scalar loops (no FMA fusion across scalar ops) and ~4x faster.
Micro-benchmark gotcha: comparing loop outputs where one buffer is np.empty (uninitialized) fabricates bitwise mismatches — always np.full(nan) both sides before diffing recurrence chains.

killpg(os.getpgid(pid)) on a worker sharing the supervisor's group SIGTERMs the whole orchestrator group; and os.kill(0/-n, SIGTERM) is itself a group broadcast, so a 'kill pid only' fallback must still refuse pid<1 (and pid==self = supervisor suicide). Mutation-check these by running pytest in its own session (subprocess start_new_session=True) or the mutant takes out your shell too.

killpg(getpgid(pid)) is unsafe whenever the target is not its own group leader: background jobs from a non-interactive shell (no job control) all share the shell's pgid, so killing one worker kills its siblings and the launcher. Use killpg only when getpgid(pid)==pid; demonstrated on stall_watch ca1d573 (/tmp/rev-w8/sibling.py).

Synthetic TradeTicks as NT fill-release events: (1) tick size is L1 liquidity -> size 0.001 caused partial fills + REDUCE_ONLY rejects; use a huge size. (2) With a LatencyModel on strategy-TF bars, SL/TP brackets submitted after the entry fill stay inflight until the NEXT data event -> one tick per bar leaves the first bar unprotected (239: 1.235 vs 0.797); a 2nd tick at T+2m releases them and reproduces 1m-detail screening bit-identically (239, 241, churner).

Churner PP-short 4h: current 3.94/46 vs val 0.19/87; ticks 0.34/87. Release ticks = 2 TradeTicks/strategy bar (close of 1m bars at T, T+1m, at their ts_init) + CLOUD latency.

NT docs: 'The engine does not provide a native next-bar-open fill mode'; bar-only latency releases an order only after the next bar's full OHLC sweep (fills at its close); ticks release earlier. delay=0 fill at close[t] is NOT look-ahead per NT docs (acting on a completed bar) - it is the zero-latency fill; 239 with open-of-first-1m ticks = 0.920 (~ immediate 0.915), i.e. validation's 1m-close fill costs 239 ~0.12 Sharpe vs real first-trade fills.

Prefix-memo prototype (/tmp/perf1m/memo_proto.py): memoize _rma_np on a bitwise input-prefix check (len+1, uint64 view equal) and extend by one recurrence step -> compute_adx 792->126 us/call, bit-identical over 19,989 real BTC 1m buffer frames (cap 1330, 25% slack trims, 2 zero-range bars). Needs >=4 slots per length (ATR/+DM/-DM/DX share the length key, one slot thrashes = 0 gain).

NT latency release is VENUE-wide: _process_and_settle_venues drains every inflight order after ANY instrument's data event (engine.pyx:1722, 3649). In a multi-symbol shared-venue run, symbol B's order is released by symbol A's same-ts tick/1m bar and fills at B's stale book = SIGNAL CLOSE. Measured 239 BTC+ETH 2024: release-ticks screening ETH 48/49 market fills at signal close (BTC 24/24 at own tick); VALIDATION 1m detail ETH 41/49 at signal close (BTC 19/24 t1). Probes /tmp/rev-fill/multi.py, vmulti.py.

NT BacktestDataConfig for an instrument missing from the catalog only WARNs ('Requested instrument_ids ... not found in catalog') and the run proceeds - a missing fill-tick catalog silently reverts 239 to next-bar-close fills (sharpe 0.52/23 vs 0.99/24, plus REDUCE_ONLY rejects). Any synthetic-data feed needs an explicit fail-closed coverage check per symbol+window.

Release-ticks vs 1m-detail on 239: sharpe/trades/return/PF bit-identical but max DD differs (0.0572 vs 0.0607) because MTM DD walks execution-TF bars (4h vs 1m). Don't claim full bit-identity. Also NT process_bar re-processes the strategy bar OPEN as a gap tick after release ticks moved last price (engine.pyx _process_trade_bar_open, fill_at_market=True), so resting SL/TP can fill at a pre-entry price.

reviewer.md design mode: add 'For any change to engine fill timing/latency, probe a 2-symbol shared-venue run (one engine, default portfolio mode) and classify each symbol's fills' - evidence: 8gfmf design review, release-ticks put ETH 48/49 fills at the signal close; all 6 architect measurements were single-symbol.

KAMA and ADX outputs are NOT prefix-stable: the whole-window non_zero_range eps guard ((diff==0).any() -> +eps to every element) means appending ONE bar with a zero diff/zero range changes earlier outputs (KAMA 290/400, ADX 98/287; /tmp/rev-perf/{kama,adx}_flip.py). Any prefix memo must key on the recurrence's actual inputs (rma input arrays, KAMA sc+c after the pandas rolling sum), compared bitwise, never on the df/close prefix.

Recurrence-memo v2 (/tmp/perf1m/memo_v2.py, flip_check.py): memoize only the pure recurrence (rma / KAMA (sc,c) / FRAMA (h,l,c) / MACD _ema_aligned) on its actual inputs, compared bitwise, with one shared step helper. Full output array bit-identical to the reference on every frame of a real BTC 1m stream (20k bars, trims, 5 zero-range bars, 85 equal closes, NaN gaps, 2+2 forced mid-segment eps flips). Per call: ADX 868->192us (4.5x), KAMA 356->139 (2.6x), FRAMA 2062->123 (16.8x), MACD 675->104 (6.5x).

perf memo_v2 r2: bit-identical full arrays (20k+16k BTC 1m, flips, NaN, interleaved 2 symbols x ADX14/14/20; /tmp/rev-perf/attack_v2.py). Perf trap: lookup keeps the matched n-1 entry as a stale slot, so 8 slots hold only 4 live series; 2 series same rma length -> hits 369/misses 2595 vs 2952/8 when the matched entry is replaced on hit (/tmp/rev-perf/slots_v2.py).
